question: How does the national health insurance thing work for foreign students in Korea?
required_facts: International students must join National Health Insurance (mandatory since March 2021)
NHIS mails the bill to the address on the Alien Registration Card; pay monthly by the deadline (auto-transfer possible)
Monthly premium from March 1, 2026: 79,320 won
Late or missing payment hurts visa/stay extension; up to 5% late fees and limited benefits
reference_answer: National Health Insurance is mandatory for international students in Korea (since March 2021). The NHIS sends a monthly bill to the address on your Alien Registration Card and you pay it by the deadline (auto-transfer is possible); from March 1, 2026 the premium is 79,320 won a month. With NHI you pay only part of the cost (20% inpatient, 30-60% outpatient) and need no claim; unpaid premiums hurt stay-extension reviews and add up to 5% late fees.
notes: National rule; ERICA NHI page and Seoul notices agree. Persona is applicant but the question does not state it (scope default). 2025 premium notice outdated.

question: Is there a private insurance option besides the national one? Not sure what the pages say.
required_facts: Yes, the university runs a private/group insurance separate from NHI
Seoul: enrolled students' premium is paid fully by the university budget (completed-coursework students pay 25,000 won themselves)
ERICA: university group insurance, KRW 25,000 per semester, charged on the tuition bill
reference_answer: Yes, besides National Health Insurance the university has its own private insurance. At Seoul, enrolled students are covered and the premium is paid in full by the university budget (students who completed coursework pay 25,000 won themselves). At ERICA, the university group insurance costs KRW 25,000 per semester and is charged on your tuition bill.
notes: Campus unstated; who pays differs by campus. academic_status splits only inside Seoul; enrolled covers the persona, given as a caveat.

question: What documents do I need to prepare before I can do a part-time job?
required_facts: Part-time Work Confirmation Form signed by the university's person in charge of international students
Copy of Alien Registration Card, employment contract and copy of the employer's Business Registration Certificate
Transcript or Certificate of Enrollment and proof of Korean (or English) proficiency
reference_answer: Before starting a part-time job you need a part-time work permit. Prepare the Part-time Work Confirmation Form (signed by the university's person in charge of international students), a copy of your Alien Registration Card, the employment contract, a copy of the employer's Business Registration Certificate, a transcript or certificate of enrollment, and proof of Korean (or English) proficiency, plus the application form and passport. The work may start only after the permit is granted.
notes: Immigration permit, national; Seoul checklist and ERICA visa page list the same documents. Visiting D-2-8 6-month wait (ERICA page) is an eligibility caveat, not about documents.

question: Hi, is there some kind of compulsory education that international students must take?

question: What is the psychological health test for international students and why is it done?
required_facts: Seoul: a short PHQ-9 test (1-2 minutes) to check your mental health over the past two weeks
Seoul: voluntary and confidential; a counselor contacts you only if extra support seems needed
ERICA: screening tests and mental-health check-ups for new students to prevent problems and help adaptation
reference_answer: At Seoul, the psychological health test is the PHQ-9, a 1-2 minute questionnaire on HY-in that checks your mental health over the past two weeks; it is voluntary and confidential, and a counselor emails you only if extra support seems needed. At ERICA, new students take group screening tests (SDS/SAS) and mental-health check-ups as part of the 3-phase counseling service, to prevent problems early and help them adapt.
notes: Campus unstated; the two campuses describe different tests and purposes.

question: Difference between exchange student program and the visiting student program?
required_facts: Exchange: for students officially nominated by partner universities; fee-waived
Visiting: fee-paying, open to international students who want to study at Hanyang
Both last one or two regular semesters
reference_answer: The Student Exchange Program is for students officially nominated by a Hanyang partner university; they study one or two regular semesters as fee-waived students. The Visiting Student Program is fee-paying and open to any international student who wants to study at Hanyang for one or two regular semesters.

question: how do I apply for scholarships
required_facts: The main international scholarship (HIEA) is applied for online through the HY-in portal by the student
Applications open each semester (early March / early September) in a set window
Upload a TOPIK (or IELTS/TOEFL for English track) certificate and pay tuition; no paper screening or interview
reference_answer: Apply online yourself through the HY-in portal: International Students > International Scholarship Application > choose the semester > Hanyang International Excellence Scholarship (HIEA) > Apply. Applications open each semester (early March and early September; 2026-1 was March 10-24); upload your TOPIK certificate (IELTS/TOEFL for English-track students) and pay tuition on time. There is no paper screening or interview; GPA is the main criterion.
notes: Both campuses use HY-in for HIEA, so campus does not change the answer's value. TOPIK scholarships have separate notices.

question: Any safety advice for crowded places this season?
required_facts: Avoid crowded areas such as Itaewon, Hongdae and Seongsu during Halloween (esp. Saturday, Oct 31, 2026)
Stay away from narrow alleys, stairways and entrances; leave if the crowd grows
Follow police/safety staff; in an emergency call 112 (police) or 119

question: What does the OIA do for international students?

Handles international inquiries; supports international students (ERICA OIA: admissions and support services)
reference_answer: The OIA is Hanyang's liaison with the global community. It runs study abroad and student exchange, short-term study (including language learning) and degree study for international students, and the International Summer and Winter Schools, and it handles international inquiries. At ERICA, the OIA likewise handles international admissions and support services for international students.

question: Is there a free Korean class run by volunteers?

question: What is the GKS-G university track and what forms does it need?
required_facts: GKS-G is the Global Korea Scholarship for graduate degrees; under the University Track you apply directly to ONE university and ONE department
At Hanyang (2026): online form 2026.02.11-03.03, then documents in person or by post to International Building #218, document screening and Zoom interview

reference_answer: The GKS-G is the Korean government's Global Korea Scholarship for graduate degrees; in the University Track you apply directly to one university and one department instead of through an embassy. The forms are the Application Form, Personal Statement, Study Plan, one Letter of Recommendation, GKS Applicant Agreement, Personal Medical Assessment and the personal-information consent, plus certificates (diplomas, transcripts, citizenship proof); research applicants add a research proposal and letter of invitation.
notes: Latest is the 2026 guideline; older GKS-G years outdated.

question: What kind of events or programs does ERICA offer to support international students?
required_facts: Field programs to attractions and traditional culture (1-2 per semester; apply at the OIA Welcome Desk)
Free K-Movie Night with English subtitles (1-2 per semester)
Hanmille peer mentoring program for new international students
GLOBAL LOVE HYU student group; also the 3-phase counseling service

Free psychological counseling is also available.

question: What scholarships exist at ERICA?
required_facts: HIEA (Hanyang International Excellence Awards): 30/50/70/100% of one semester's tuition, by GPA (80%) and TOPIK (20%), apply on HY-in
TOPIK Scholarship: KRW 500,000-1,000,000 for improving your TOPIK level (excludes leave, extra-semester and completed students)
Dormitory/floor representative subsidies (50%/30%) and GLOBAL LOVE HYU scholarship (up to KRW 1,000,000)
reference_answer: ERICA offers the Hanyang International Excellence Awards (HIEA), which cover 30%, 50%, 70% or 100% of one semester's tuition based on GPA (80%) and TOPIK (20%), and the TOPIK Scholarship, KRW 500,000-1,000,000 for students who raise their TOPIK level. Dormitory and floor representatives get 50% and 30% dorm-fee subsidies, and GLOBAL LOVE HYU members can receive up to KRW 1,000,000. Note that the TOPIK Scholarship excludes students on leave, in extra semesters and students who completed coursework, and HIEA requires current registration.
notes: Gold persona completed coursework: excluded from the TOPIK scholarship and HIEA requires registration; stated as caveats (question asks what exists).

question: Who can I talk to if I feel really down while studying here?
required_facts: Seoul: the OIA counseling program (individual counseling); visit or e-mail the OIA, 02-2220-2450, International Building 218
ERICA: international student counseling center, 031-400-4926 (English/Korean), Mon-Fri 10:00-17:00; book on HY-in
In a crisis call 112 or 1577-1366 (24h, 13 languages)

At ERICA, contact the international student counseling center (031-400-4926 English/Korean, Mon-Fri 10:00-17:00) or book through HY-in. If you are in crisis, call 112 or 1577-1366 (24 hours, interpretation in 13 languages).
notes: Campus unstated (persona ERICA); offices differ.

Seoul: individual counseling and tests (MBTI, SCT, MMPI) through the OIA; apply by visiting or e-mailing the OIA

At ERICA, the international student counseling center offers 1-on-1 counseling (up to 12 sessions of 45 minutes) and psychological tests such as MMPI-2, SCT, MBTI, TCI, FCPI and Holland, in English, Chinese or Korean; book on HY-in > Application > Personal Counseling/Psychological Testing. At Seoul, the OIA offers individual counseling and tests (MBTI, SCT, MMPI); apply by visiting or e-mailing the OIA.
notes: Campus unstated (persona ERICA); booking routes differ.

question: Any group counseling or workshops for students?

ERICA: one-off workshops (DIY handicraft, meditation, color therapy), 2 per semester

reference_answer: Yes. notes: Campus unstated (persona ERICA).

question: What does the university group insurance cover?
required_facts: Coverage period: 1st semester Mar 1-Sep 1, 2nd semester Sep 1-Mar 1
Covers death/after-effects from injury or disease, reimbursable and non-reimbursable medical expenses, personal liability, overseas hospitalization, special expenses for foreigners
Non-reimbursable items covered include manual therapy, shock-wave therapy, injections, MRI/MRA; premium KRW 25,000 per semester
reference_answer: The ERICA university group insurance runs per semester (Mar 1-Sep 1 and Sep 1-Mar 1) and costs KRW 25,000. It covers death and after-effects from injury or disease, reimbursable and non-reimbursable medical expenses for injury or sickness (e.g. manual therapy, shock-wave therapy, injections, MRI/MRA), personal liability, overseas hospitalization and medical expenses, and special expenses for foreigners. Claims go through the insurer's website.
notes: 'University group insurance' is ERICA's term; Seoul's private-insurance notice gives no coverage list (attachment only), so campus does not split.

question: What is alien registration and when do I have to do it?
required_facts: Foreigners staying in Korea more than 90 days must register as aliens (get an Alien Registration/Residence Card)
Register within 90 days of entry; immediately when granted a status or a change of status
Late registration means a fine; group registration via the OIA each semester, or book individually on HiKorea
reference_answer: Alien registration is the immigration registration (giving you an Alien Registration Card) that every foreigner staying in Korea more than 90 days must complete. You must register within 90 days of entering Korea, or immediately when you are granted a residence status or a change of status; missing the deadline means a fine. Check the OIA's group-registration notice each semester, or book an appointment on HiKorea and apply at the immigration office yourself.
notes: National immigration rule; ERICA visa page.

question: Can you explain the group visa application process?
required_facts: Seoul: applying in person is the rule, but the OIA offers group visa (D-4->D-2 change, D-2 extension) and group residence-card applications

Seoul: from abroad, get the Certificate of Admission (overseas use), get the D-2 at the embassy, enter, then apply for the group residence card; in Korea, use the domestic-use certificate and the group visa (change mid-Aug, extension mid-Aug to mid-Sep)
ERICA: group registrations are announced in OIA notices each semester (guide as attachment); otherwise book on HiKorea and apply individually
reference_answer: At Seoul, applying in person at immigration is the rule, but the OIA runs group applications: if you are abroad, receive the Certificate of Admission (overseas use), get your D-2 visa at the Korean embassy, enter Korea and join the group residence-card application; if you are in Korea, use the domestic-use certificate and join the group visa application (status change mid-August, extension mid-August to mid-September); new alien registration through the group costs a discounted KRW 25,000. At ERICA, group registrations are announced in the OIA notices each semester (the guide is an attachment); otherwise book on HiKorea and apply at the immigration office yourself.
notes: Campus unstated (persona ERICA). ERICA's 2025 group visa guide is attachment-only (11.2), so the ERICA branch gives only the notice route.

question: Why study at ERICA instead of the main campus?
required_facts: ERICA (Ansan) is Korea's leading campus for industry-academia cooperation; 143-200+ companies on campus
Education combines research with business and hands-on training
1st in Korea (6th worldwide) for Industry-Innovation-Infrastructure (THE Impact Rankings 2022); 600 partner universities in 70 countries
reference_answer: ERICA, in Ansan, is known as Korea's most active campus for industry-academia cooperation: more than 140 companies are on campus and work with students and faculty, and teaching combines research with hands-on industry training. It ranked 1st in Korea (6th worldwide) for Industry-Innovation-Infrastructure in the 2022 THE Impact Rankings and offers exchange and other programs with about 600 partner universities in 70 countries.
notes: Pages do not compare with Seoul directly; answer gives ERICA's stated strengths.

question: What are outgoing programs and what are the benefits?
required_facts: Outgoing (exchange) programs: study a set period at a partner university abroad while paying tuition only to Hanyang
Credits earned abroad transfer on return (up to 20 per semester, up to 1/2 of graduation credits)
Requirements: enrolled or on leave at ERICA, cumulative GPA 2.5/4.5; graduate students need supervisor approval
reference_answer: Outgoing programs let you study for a period at a partner university abroad while paying tuition only to Hanyang. The credits you earn there are transferred on return, up to 20 credits a semester and up to half of the credits needed to graduate. Graduate students apply if enrolled (or on leave) at ERICA, with at least 1 completed semester, supervisor approval and a cumulative GPA of 2.5/4.5 or higher.
notes: ERICA pages; the 'Advantages' heading has no text, so benefits come from the overview. Persona graduating doctoral; final-semester note is a caveat.

question: Can I get a scholarship?
required_facts: Depends on campus, degree level, enrollment status and TOPIK level
Seoul HIEA: enrolled more than 1 semester, GPA >= 3.0 (undergrad) / 4.2 (grad) last semester, valid TOPIK (or IELTS/TOEFL for English track); not on leave or completed
Seoul TOPIK scholarship: enrolled degree students with TOPIK 5 or 6; ERICA HIEA and TOPIK scholarship have their own rules
reference_answer: Which campus are you at, and are you an undergraduate or a graduate student? For example, at Seoul the HIEA needs at least one completed semester, a last-semester GPA of 3.0 (undergraduate) or 4.2 (graduate) and a valid TOPIK (or IELTS/TOEFL for English-track students), and the TOPIK scholarship needs TOPIK level 5 or 6; students on leave or who have completed coursework cannot apply. ERICA has its own HIEA and TOPIK-scholarship rules.
notes: Many branches (campus x degree x status x TOPIK) -> clarify; campus splits the evidence most. GPA is a caveat.

question: How do I take a break from my studies and come back later?
required_facts: Seoul: leave-of-absence notice posted on the OIA board each semester; one year at a time (max 3 years, undergrad); re-register online in the re-registration period or be dismissed
Seoul re-registration: online only (no in-person/e-mail), passport copy and bank balance certificate (USD 16,000 / KRW 20,000,000)
ERICA: apply for leave on HY-in (upload passport and RC); leave Korea within 30 days; max 1 year at a time
ERICA: return-to-school application in set rounds; mail the original bank balance certificate to the ERICA OIA
reference_answer: At Seoul, the OIA posts the leave-of-absence notice each semester (2026-1: Feb 11-19); undergraduates take one year at a time, up to 3 years. To come back you must re-register online during the re-registration period (2026-1: Jan 5-16) with a passport copy and a bank balance certificate (USD 16,000 or KRW 20,000,000); in-person or e-mail applications are not accepted, and not re-registering when the leave ends means dismissal. At ERICA, apply for leave on HY-in (upload your passport and RC) and leave Korea within 30 days; return through the return-to-school application rounds by sending the original bank balance certificate to the ERICA OIA.
notes: Campus unstated (persona Seoul, on leave). Next-term (2027-1) dates not in snapshot; procedures are stable.

question: Do I have to join the national health insurance?
required_facts: Yes: National Health Insurance is mandatory for international students (since March 2021)
NHIS sends the bill to your ARC address; pay monthly (79,320 won from March 2026)
Exceptions: Japanese students with valid Japanese NHI can apply for exemption; language-course students ask their language school
reference_answer: Yes. Since March 2021 international students must be covered by National Health Insurance; the NHIS mails the bill to the address on your Alien Registration Card and you pay monthly (79,320 won from March 1, 2026). Japanese students with valid Japanese NHI can apply for an exemption by phoning the NHIS, and language-course students should ask their language school.
notes: National rule; no visa or student_type split in the evidence (10.2, T14-109).

question: How do I extend my stay? My card expires soon.
required_facts: Apply for extension of stay from 4 months before the card/visa expires, no later than the expiry date
Documents: application form, passport copy, ARC, certificate of enrollment, tuition receipt, last semester's transcript, proof of residence; fee KRW 60,000
Stay in Korea until the extension is approved; Seoul Immigration Office moved to 55 Jeongui-ro, Songpa-gu (from Oct 19, 2026)
reference_answer: Apply for an extension of stay from 4 months before your card expires and no later than the expiry date. Bring the application form, a passport copy, your Alien Registration Card, a certificate of enrollment, the tuition payment receipt, last semester's transcript and proof of residence, plus the KRW 60,000 fee; extra documents (bank balance, supervisor letter) apply only in special cases such as deferred graduation or low GPA. Stay in Korea until it is approved, or the extension is cancelled. The Seoul Immigration Office has moved to 55 Jeongui-ro, Songpa-gu (since October 19, 2026).
notes: National immigration rule; ERICA visa page gives the procedure. Extra-semester supervisor form (a6beb530) is a caveat.

question: Can the school apply for my visa for me?
required_facts: In principle you apply in person, but the OIA offers group visa (change/extension) and group residence-card applications
From abroad you apply for the D-2 visa yourself at the Korean embassy with the Certificate of Admission (overseas use)
Otherwise apply individually: book on HiKorea and visit the immigration office
reference_answer: Partly. The rule is that you apply in person, but for convenience the OIA runs group applications: in Korea it files group visa changes and extensions and group residence-card applications for you. If you are abroad, you apply for the D-2 visa yourself at the Korean embassy with your Certificate of Admission (overseas use), then join the group residence-card application after entry. If you prefer, apply individually by booking on HiKorea and visiting the immigration office.
notes: Persona applicant but not stated (scope default). Seoul acceptance guideline plus ERICA visa page agree on group applications.

question: Do I have to file an entry report when I arrive?
required_facts: Yes: international degree students must respond to the entry and exit report on HY-in every semester (mandatory)
Students who have not entered Korea or are on leave of absence must also respond
Update it on arrival with a passport copy, visa documents and proof of entry; not responding risks visa cancellation or entry refusal
reference_answer: Yes. International degree students must answer the entry and exit report on the HY-in portal every semester, and students who are on leave of absence or not yet in Korea must answer too. When you arrive, update it with a passport copy, your visa documents and proof of entry (e.g. boarding pass or entry label). Not responding can lead to visa cancellation or entry refusal.
notes: Seoul notices (latest 2022-06); stable rule. 2021 notice superseded.

question: Do I need a TOPIK score to study here?
required_facts: Depends on whether you are a degree-seeking or an exchange/visiting student
Degree-seeking undergraduates must meet (or be exempt from) the Korean language standard, e.g. TOPIK 4+ or Hanyang IIE level 4+
If not met: placed on leave for the first semester, study Korean (D-4), then re-register
Exchange/visiting language requirements are not in the snapshot
reference_answer: Are you coming as a degree-seeking student or as an exchange/visiting student? For degree-seeking undergraduates, admission checks a Korean language standard (TOPIK level 4 or Hanyang IIE level 4, unless you are exempt); students who do not meet it are placed on leave for the first semester, study Korean, and re-register once they meet it. The snapshot does not state a TOPIK requirement for exchange or visiting students, so they should ask the OIA.

question: Do I have to take that psychological test?
required_facts: No: the psychological health test is voluntary
It is a short PHQ-9 check (1-2 minutes) on HY-in, results confidential
A counselor contacts you only if extra support seems needed
reference_answer: No. The psychological health test is completely voluntary. It is a 1-2 minute PHQ-9 questionnaire on HY-in that checks your mental health over the past two weeks; results are confidential and only a counseling professional sees them, contacting you by e-mail only if extra support seems needed.
notes: Seoul notice (2026-1) says voluntary; ERICA new-student screening page does not say mandatory or voluntary, so no campus split. 2023 notice ('asking each and every one') superseded in tone.

question: Is the compulsory education mandatory for me?
required_facts: The 2026 compulsory education is required for all enrolled international students
Complete it online via the hylu-s course link by Sunday, September 13, 2026
The notice does not cover students on leave of absence; check with the OIA
reference_answer: The 2026 Mandatory Education for International Students must be completed by all enrolled international students, online through the hylu-s course link, by Sunday, September 13, 2026. The notice speaks only of enrolled students, so as a student on leave of absence you are not clearly covered; confirm with the OIA.

question: Am I eligible for the GKS scholarship?
required_facts: The GKS in the snapshot is GKS-G, for graduate degrees: you need a bachelor's degree (master's) or master's (doctoral), or expect it by July 31, 2026
Citizenship of an invited country (parents not Korean), under 40, CGPA >= 80% / 2.64 of 4.0, good health
Not eligible if you graduated from a Korean high school/university or previously received a Korean government degree scholarship
reference_answer: The GKS described in the snapshot is the GKS-G for graduate degrees, so as an undergraduate you qualify only if you will hold a bachelor's degree by July 31, 2026 (the 2026 round). Applicants need citizenship of a GKS-invited country (parents not Korean), a CGPA of at least 80% or 2.64/4.0, must be under 40 and in good health, and must not have graduated from a Korean high school or university or held a Korean government degree scholarship. Former GKS exchange-program scholars can apply.
notes: Persona undergrad year 3 exchange -> not eligible yet; degree held is the deciding fact (caveat). Next round's dates not published.
